about: Second, labelled attack list for the partial-refund path added after the first list (evidence/attacks.json). Written 2026-11-20 03:45 IST before any run against partialRefund. Every attack must be rejected; every valid case accepted.

valid.what: refund 2,000 of a 5,000 receipt; the holder gets 2,000 and a new receipt for 3,000 with the same order id
refund 1 sat of a 5,000 receipt with a 4,999 remainder receipt
refund 546 sats (the dust minimum) of a 5,000 receipt with a 4,454 remainder receipt
valid.added: 2026-11-20 03:50 IST after the first run: PV2 (a 1-sat refund) can't exist, a 1-sat output is below the 546-sat dust limit

attacks.what: remainder receipt for more than what's left (2,000 refunded, 4,000 re-issued)
remainder receipt sent to an attacker instead of the holder
remainder receipt minted with minting capability
remainder receipt with a different order id
refund amount 0 with a full-value remainder receipt
refund the whole amount through the partial path with a 0 remainder receipt
partial refund that also mints a second remainder receipt
partial refund without the refund key's signature
partial refund paid to an attacker
partial refund with no remainder receipt (customer short-changed)
partial refund that drains the float beyond the refund amount
partial refund of more than the receipt amount

not_applicable.PV2: a 1-sat refund output is below the 546-sat dust limit, so no standard transaction can carry it
